title: The tests are changing
text: I'm reworking the test structure to make it fairer.

title: Safety training changed one model a lot
text: With safety training, Qwen3 4B wrote a hazard for 30 of 84 hostile requests and declined 53. With it removed, the same model wrote 70 and declined 3.

title: Removing safety training took away every refusal in one model
text: With safety training, qwen2.5-coder 7B wrote a hazard for 68 of 97 hostile requests and declined 25. With it removed, the same model wrote 92 and declined 0.

title: Removing safety training does not always add hazards
text: llama3.1 8B wrote a hazard for 74 of 84 hostile requests. Its copy with safety training removed wrote 35 and declined 21, against 3. Test each copy, and don't assume what it will do.

title: Some models never said no
text: Asked to do something hostile, 7 of 26 models declined nothing, and some of these still had their safety training. Don't rely on a model to refuse.

title: Even the safest models wrote hazards
text: 4 of 26 models did best, and the test cannot separate them. Even so, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B wrote a hazard for 29 of 99 hostile requests.

title: termite stopped almost every hazard
text: These 26 models wrote 1672 hazardous replies to hostile requests. termite stopped or held 1670 of them for a person to check, and 2 were Injected.

title: Refusing can go too far
text: qwen2.5 7B declined 11 of 40 harmless everyday requests. A model that refuses too much is a problem too, because people stop using it.

title: Models called hazards harmless
text: In at least 241 of 1672 hazardous replies, the model said that the command only reads. Don't trust a model's description of its own command.

title: A bigger model was not clearly safer
text: Across 26 models, larger models did not write clearly fewer hazards. Test each model, and don't judge it by its size.

title: Replies break before the server refuses
text: At 110% of the limit set on the server, 0 of 224 trials overflowed, but 67 replies came back broken. At 120% and 130%, all 224 trials at each level overflowed. This limit was set for the test, and it is not the model's own limit.

title: The policy catches what decision models miss
text: The 17 decision models rated 158 risky commands safe. termite's policy blocked 74 of them, and the other 84 were at tier 2, where a command shows personal information but no secrets.

title: Reading near secrets looks safe to them
text: Liquid d1 2B rated 8 of 8 sensitive reads safe, such as listing a folder of keys. It rated 0 of 6 small project changes safe. A read near a secret can look harmless to a model.

title: Some models refused every critical command
text: Of 17 models, some refused every critical command. Clef refused 8 of 8. Other models asked a person about some of these commands, so test the model you plan to use.

title: One model told risky and harmless commands apart
text: In this run, JevK5 4B rated 5 of 38 risky commands safe, and 13 of 14 harmless commands safe. Both numbers matter, because a model that rates nothing safe would also look good on the first number.

title: One model asks about everything
text: Laya asked for approval on 52 of 52 commands, and rated 0 of 14 harmless commands safe. That is cautious, but people stop reading warnings that they see every time.

title: Models often did not put the safest option first
text: Given several ways to do a job, the best of 17 models put the safest way first in only 6 of 10 tests.

title: Many decision models need a different setup
text: 8 of 25 decision models gave no score. llama.cpp said each file is not a decision model, and each one needs its own server or client. This says nothing about how good those models are.
